title: Lesson 49 - I've Been Working on It

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: How is the greeter briefing going? Priya needs an internal-review copy tomorrow afternoon.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I've been working on it since Monday. I've been checking the arrival steps against Sam's logistics note and the wayfinding plan.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: What have you completed so far?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So far, I've drafted the welcome section, the entrance directions and the service-desk position. I've also turned the first-hour duties into a five-step sequence.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Have you added the break handoff?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Not yet. I'm still waiting on the backup-greeter contact and the confirmed time when the accessible side entrance will open.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Does that stop the whole draft?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: No. The main blocker is only the final handoff box. The rest is ready for a content check.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Good. Sometimes “waiting” makes an update sound as if nothing has moved.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That's why I'm separating the completed sections from the open inputs.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: What evidence can Priya review today?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I've uploaded version 0.6 to the internal folder. It has one page, five numbered steps and role-based contacts instead of personal numbers.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: And what have you been doing about the missing information?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I've asked Sam to confirm the entrance time, and Priya is checking which volunteer can cover the first break.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: When will you know whether those inputs are available?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Sam said he'd reply by three today. Priya will update the volunteer field by ten tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I see your point about keeping the review moving, but a blank contact box won't work for the final version.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Agreed. What I can agree to is a review draft today with a clearly marked placeholder. If we need the final PDF, we'll need both inputs first.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: What's your next checkpoint?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I'll post another status update at three thirty: completed changes, remaining blocker and whether tomorrow's four o'clock review is still on track.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Perfect. That gives us progress, evidence, a dependency and a next update—not just “I've been working on it.”
